statement: (i) Find the general solution of $\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}-3\frac{dy}{dx}+2y=0$. (ii) Find the particular solution with $y(0)=0$, $y'(0)=1$. (iii) Describe its behaviour as $x\to-\infty$ and as $x\to\infty$.
solution: (i) Characteristic equation $r^{2}-3r+2=0$ gives $r=1,2$; general solution $y=Ae^{x}+Be^{2x}$. (ii) $y(0)=A+B=0\Rightarrow B=-A$. $y'=Ae^{x}+2Be^{2x}$; $y'(0)=A+2B=1\Rightarrow A-2A=1\Rightarrow A=-1,B=1$. So $y=e^{2x}-e^{x}$. (iii) As $x\to-\infty$, both terms $\to0$, so $y\to0$. As $x\to\infty$, $e^{2x}$ dominates, so $y\to\infty$.
